title: Write-before-ioctl for key import avoids stack overflow on PQ keys
description: KEY_IMPORT uses write(2)-before-ioctl: raw key bytes are written to the fd's inbuf, then CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_KEY_IMPORT is called with a small metadata struct (algo, provider, key_type, exportable, keylen — no key bytes). The ioctl comment documents the rationale explicitly: RSA-4096 PKCS#8 is ~2.4 KB, ML-DSA-87 is 4896 bytes. Embedding key bytes in the ioctl struct would require a worst-case 8192-byte struct on the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call — violating the ~1 KB kernel stack frame guideline and causing stack overflow on PQ key imports. The write-before-ioctl pattern allocates exactly what the key requires on the heap via inbuf, then zeroizes (memzero_explicit) and frees after import. A reviewer might suggest 'just embed the key in the struct with a large fixed buffer — it's simpler.' That approach cannot be corrected later without an ABI break, and it will overflow the stack for ML-DSA keys today.
